# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 4
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf has not spoken to me in two rounds. Please gesture to Deaf: tell Deaf to SPEAK the wire colours and which wire to cut, out loud, so I can hear it. I am the only one who can cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot read the manual, so I cannot decode your gesture code. Please give me the wire number by finger count: one finger for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, three fingers for wire 3. Current state: display 0, light green, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

Deaf says: cannot read the manual, cannot decode my gesture code. Wants the wire number by finger count: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3. Current state: display 0, light green, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

0 yellow flashes → blue → wire 3. So I gesture 🤟 (three fingers) to mean wire 3.

Also, Blind is asking Deaf to speak the wire colors and which wire to cut out loud. Deaf can speak. So once Deaf knows wire 3, Deaf will speak it to Blind.

I'll gesture 🤟 to Deaf. Maybe also ✊ to confirm blue, but Deaf can't decode color symbols. Just 🤟 is enough: wire 3.

Let me send: gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"]).

Actually, Deaf explicitly asked for finger count. So 🤟 = 3 = wire 3. That's the answer.

Let me send just that. Maybe also a confirmation 👍? But Deaf might not need it. I'll send 🤟 and maybe 👍.

Let me send: gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"]).

Wait, should I also tell Deaf to speak to Blind? Deaf already knows to relay. Blind asked Deaf to speak. Deaf will speak once it knows. So just the wire number.

I'll send 🤟.

Let me write the response.Deaf can't decode my color code but can read finger counts: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3. Current state: display 0 yellow flashes, light green, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

0 yellow flashes → blue → wire 3. So I gesture 🤟 (three fingers) to tell Deaf: cut wire 3. Deaf can then speak "wire 3" (or "blue") to Blind, who can hear and cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

gone, unless someone says it again.)

Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Received from Deaf: display 0, light green, wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue. Waiting on the manual's wire number. Please send it to Deaf so Deaf can speak it to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I read your 🤟 as three fingers = wire 3. But the light has changed again: it is now yellow, display still 0, wires 1 green 2 red 3 blue. Confirm: is wire 3 correct for the yellow light, display 0? If yes, gesture 🤟 again.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟]

Deaf read 🤟 as wire 3 and is asking for confirmation. Current state: display 0, light yellow (changed back from green), wires 1 green, 2 red, 3 blue.

0 yellow flashes → blue → wire 3. So yes, wire 3 is correct. I confirm by gesturing 🤟 again.

Deaf will then speak "wire 3" (or "blue") to Blind, who can cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:

yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Deaf reports the light changed and is confirming with you. I am holding, ready to cut on Deaf's final word. Please give Deaf the wire number the manual dictates for display 0 with the current light and wire colours.
Deaf says to Mute: Confirmed: wire 3. I am telling Blind to cut wire 3, the blue one.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟]

Deaf has confirmed: wire 3, the blue one, and is telling Blind to cut. Blind is holding, ready to cut on Deaf's final word.

Everything is aligned: display 0 yellow flashes → blue → wire 3. Deaf has the correct answer and is relaying it to Blind. Nothing more is needed from me — I have no further information to add, and any extra gesture risks confusion.

I'll wait.

```
wait()
```
